info.name: PayTrack API
info.description:
PayTrack microservices test collection.

Architecture:
- paytrack-gateway: Spring Cloud Gateway (http://localhost:8085) — routes ONLY /api/payments/**
- payment-service: REST API (host 8082 in Docker) — /api/payments/** and /api/accounts/**
- fraud-service: Kafka-driven, NO REST API
- paytrack-registry: Eureka (http://localhost:8761)
- paytrack-config: Config Server (http://localhost:8888)
- kafka-ui: Kafka UI (http://localhost:8090)

Routing note: the gateway currently declares a single route for /api/payments/** (paytrack-gateway/application.yaml). Account and stats endpoints under /api/accounts/** must be called DIRECTLY on payment-service ({{paymentServiceUrl}}).

Workflow hint: accounts start with balance 0 — to test transfers successfully, UPDATE the balance in the paymentdb accounts table (e.g. `UPDATE accounts SET balance = 1000 WHERE account_number = '<ACC-...>';`), otherwise every transfer fails with 'Insufficient balance'.

Setup: `docker compose up --build`, then import this collection and the 'PayTrack Local' environment.

Actuator: payment-service now exposes /actuator/health|info|metrics|loggers|env (management config in paytrack-config/configurations). Rebuild the images after the pom change: docker compose up --build.

item.name: Accounts
item.description:
Account management under /api/accounts/**. NOT routed by the gateway (only /api/payments/** is), so call payment-service directly on {{paymentServiceUrl}}. Account numbers are auto-generated (ACC-########). New accounts start with balance = 0, status = ACTIVE. The {{accountId}} and {{accountNumber}} variables are set automatically by "Create Account".

Lifecycle: ACTIVE -> deactivate -> INACTIVE, ACTIVE/INACTIVE -> block -> BLOCKED, unblock -> ACTIVE. An account can only be closed (DELETE or POST /close) when its balance is zero. Deposit/withdraw mutate the balance directly. The statement lists payments where the account is the source (DEBIT) or destination (CREDIT).

item.name: Create Account

request.description: Creates an account. Expected 201 CREATED with AccountDto (auto-generated accountNumber, balance=0, status=ACTIVE). Stores accountNumber to the {{accountNumber}} variable.

item.description: Creates an account. Expected 201 CREATED with AccountDto (auto-generated accountNumber, balance=0, status=ACTIVE, currency=MAD). Stores id -> {{accountId}} and accountNumber -> {{accountNumber}}.

request.description: Expected 400: 'An account already exists with this email'. Run 'Create Account' first, or adapt the email.
Bean validation: `@Email` on ownerEmail and `@Size(min=3,max=3)` on currency.

query.description: Optional. One of: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, BLOCKED, CLOSED

Fetch a single account by UUID ({{accountId}}), set by "Create Account". Returns AccountDto.
Fetch an account by its auto-generated number ({{accountNumber}}).
Fetch an account by the unique owner email. Expected 400 if it does not exist.
Full update. Only non-null fields are applied. Expected 200 with updated AccountDto.

Soft-closes the account (status -> CLOSED). Requires balance = 0, otherwise 400/409. Returns 204 No Content.
ACTIVE transition. Only valid from INACTIVE (use /unblock from BLOCKED). Returns AccountDto.
INACTIVE transition. Only valid from ACTIVE. Returns AccountDto.
BLOCKED transition. Only valid from ACTIVE/INACTIVE (used by fraud flows). Returns AccountDto.
ACTIVE transition from BLOCKED. Returns AccountDto.
CLOSED transition (same rule as DELETE: balance must be 0). Returns AccountDto.
Credits the account balance (amount > 0). Accounts start at 0 — use this to fund wallets for transfer tests. Returns AccountDto with the new balance.
Debits the account balance. Only ACTIVE accounts; amount must be <= balance. Returns AccountDto with the new balance.
Live balance snapshot: accountNumber, ownerName, balance, currency, status, updatedAt.
Paginated statement of payments involving the account (source = DEBIT, destination = CREDIT). Query: page, size, sort.

item.name: Fraud Service
item.description: fraud-service exposes NO REST endpoints. It consumes `payment.initiated` (via fraud.fraud-check flow), evaluates the transaction (FraudDecision APPROVED/REJECTED), and publishes the result back for payment-service to finalize. Use kafka-ui (http://localhost:8090) to inspect topics: payment.initiated, payment.processed, payment.failed, payment.DLT, payment.fraud, fraud.fraud-check, fraud.fraud-evaluated.
